units.translation: ⟦1⟧; since ⟦2⟧ and ⟦3⟧ are related (Weckl.), one should not, with others, seek the apodosis only in ⟦4⟧ V. 29.
First among the gods I honor Gaia, the first prophet

⟦1⟧ as at (7.) 784 ⟦2⟧; further 693 ⟦3⟧. 137. 174. 338 etc., ⟦4⟧. Themis is here, as in Hesiod, distinguished from Gaia and appears as her daughter (Theog. 135), while in the ⟦5⟧ A. likes to mix them: ⟦6⟧ . . ⟦7⟧, ⟦8⟧; but Themis-Gaia is also prophetic there, cf. Homer ⟦9⟧ 403 ⟦10⟧, i.e. oracles, ⟦11⟧ ⟦12⟧ (likewise); ⟦13⟧ (Apollo speaks) ⟦14⟧; Harpocration ⟦15⟧ = ⟦16⟧, attested from Lysias (GHerm.); see also on 32. So from the beginning of things there have been oracles at this site, and the deity has manifested itself ever more clearly, through ordinances and utterances that it announced to humans.
I would give unerring counsel to all
This tradition gives ⟦1⟧ from a poem bearing the name of Musaeus, Eumolpia, at any rate a product of the Pisistratid period, like other such things; cf. ⟦2⟧
⟦1⟧ as at ⟦2⟧ ⟦3⟧. ⟦4⟧ ⟦5⟧ etc.; ⟦6⟧ points to the variation in the tradition among different sources, of which Pausanias also speaks there, § 5.

Phoebe as holder only here; she too, like Themis, is one of the Hesiodic children of Uranus and Gaia, Theog. 136, and provides a particularly simple transition to the last holder ⟦1⟧. ⟦2⟧ (= ⟦3⟧ Schol.) is a word especially frequent in the Eumenides: 310. 334. 347. 386. 400 (otherwise only ⟦4⟧).

⟦1⟧: everything has taken place in a calm manner, as is fitting among gods; even the so-called Musaeus let Apollo receive the oracle from Themis as a gift. ⟦2⟧ as at ⟦3⟧ ⟦4⟧; naturally ⟦5⟧ is also one of the "many names" of Gaia, there 210, above on 2.
Titans, children of Uranus and Earth

⟦1⟧: as at V. 2; one need not, with Porson, emend to ⟦2⟧. Verses 7 and 8 are parallel in punctuation and sentence structure (Weil): ⟦3⟧· ⟦4⟧ (so M.) | ⟦5⟧ | ⟦6⟧· | ⟦7⟧ | ⟦8⟧ (- -, - -, ICI (1). Phoebe now, according to Hesiod Th. 404 ff., is mother of Leto; therefore ⟦9⟧ = ⟦10⟧, as the Schol.?
